notes: On 4 January 2019, in Buenos Aires, Ciudad Autonoma, thousands of residents, organised by several organisations including Community Movement, protested in the neighbourhoods of Caballito, Belgrano, Boedo, Mataderos, Colegiales, San Telmo and Villa Crespo took to the streets against rising prices and transport costs.
On 5 January 2020, in San Carlos de Bariloche (Rio Negro), a massive amount of people protested in the Civic Center to repudiate a man who raped a dog and to demand justice.

On 6 January 2021, in Mayor Buratovich (Buenos Aires), more than 1,000 people and MTE (Excluded Workers Movement) members marched to demand justice for a femicide case against a MTE member that took place on the previous day. The group also demanded public policies to eradicate gender-based violence.

On 4 January 2022, in Mar del Plata (Buenos Aires), more than 3,000 people from environmental and political organizations, locals, and tourists staged a demonstration on the Maritimo Peralta Ramos Boulevard against the resolution 436/2021, which authorizes a Norwegian company to do offshore oil exploitation.

On 1 January 2023, in Pergamino (Buenos Aires), a large group of people beat and kicked a vendor and his son in disagreement for the prices at their supermarket. The victims had to be taken to the hospital.

On 10 January 2024, in Mar del Plata (General Pueyrredon, Buenos Aires), thousands of artists and cultural workers protested near the General San Martin monument against the Decree of Necessity and Urgency 70/2023 (DNU), which deregulated the economy, and against the so-called Omnibus law, which proposes reforms in the State and a reduction of financing to cultural activities. The mobilization occurred within the framework of the national protest day named 'Cultural Cacerolazo.'

On 4 August 2019, in Sucre, Chuquisaca, one thousand citizens staged a demonstration to support the mayor of Ravelo, who has been arrested with charges of corruption. The demonstrators blocked the Jaime Mendoza highway for an hour.

On 24 January 2020, in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Santa Cruz, a massive number of transport workers marched towards the Secretary of Accounting (SER) offices to demonstrate against the Urban Mobility law.

On 3 January 2021, in Apolo, La Paz, a group of heavy transport workers blocked the roads leading towards the main square of the city, as a demonstration to complain about the delay of the reopening of La Paz-Charazani-Apolo highway.

On 3 February 2022, in Santa Cruz de la Sierra (Santa Cruz), 1,500 parents of students blocked kilometer 3 of La Guardia two-lane highway as a demonstration to demand the supply of educational equipment needed for teachers of La Guardia municipality.

On 5 January 2023, in Santa Cruz de la Sierra (Santa Cruz), more than 2500 transportation workers carried out a motorcade and a march around the fourth ring of the city as a demonstration to demand the release of the Santa Cruz governor (Creemos) and the stop of police repression. The Santa Cruz governor was arrested due to an investigation of his involvement in the alleged coup d'etat of 2019.

On 15 January 2024, in Santivanez (Cochabamba), at least 2,000 residents marched through the city to the local government offices as a demonstration over a gate that was installed, claiming that the borders were not respected and demanded the mayor solve this issue.

On 10 January 2019, in central Sao Paulo, Sao Paulo, approximately 15,000 people gathered at Praca Ramos de Azevedo and walked up to Rua da Consolacao and Rua Fernando de Albuquerque (impeded from getting to Avenida Paulista), to demonstrate against an increase of the public transportation fare. Near the end of the demonstration, the windows of two banks were broken and Military Police used tear gas bombs.
On 30 January 2020, in Florianopolis, Santa Catarina, about 2000 military officers and firefighters blocked SC-401 to demand salary readjustment.

On 7 January 2021, in Guaratingueta, Sao Paulo, a large group farmers drove tractors from the rural union building to the Povo Avenue, protesting with a motorcade over the increase of the tax rate on movement of agricultural goods. The protest took place even after the government announced the suspension of the measure.
On 16 February 2022, in Porto Alegre (Rio Grande do Sul), about 1,300 farmers blocked an avenue to demand financial assistance to minimize losses caused by a draught.

On 8 January 2023, in Brasilia (Distrito Federal), thousands of Bolsonaro (PL) supporters invaded buildings from the Legislative, Executive and the Judiciary, vandalized their structures, destroyed and stole historical and artistic objects, and also stole firearms from the security cabinet. The demonstrators demanded a military intervention. At least 10 journalists were verbally abused, beaten up, threatened and had their equipment stolen or destroyed by demonstrators. Military police forces dispersed the demonstrators and approximately 400 people were arrested, including civil servants, and government officials.

On 27 January 2024, in Guararema (Sao Paulo), around 1,000 MST members, political party representatives, and social movement leaders held a peaceful political act in celebration of the Landless Workers' Movement's 40 years of existence.
On 17 January 2019, in Concepcion (Biobio), 1,000 fishers staged a demonstration at La Independencia Square and Llacolen Bridge over the law regulating the fishing of cuttlefish.

On 1 January 2020, in Santiago - Providencia, Metropolitan region, a group of 10,000 people demonstrated over general discontent with the government. Rioters and Police Forces of Chile clashed when a group of demonstrators used fireworks against state forces, who reacted by throwing tear gases and water cannon at them. Police arrested six people.

On 4 January 2021, in Santiago - Providencia (Metropolitana), thousands of citizens and students demonstrated against the exam to access university education in the country, known as PCU. Demonstrators claimed the test deepens inequality in the education sector. The group clashed against police when the latter attempted to disperse demonstrators. Police arrested two people.

On 30 January 2022, in Iquique (Tarapaca), over 6,000 locals gathered at Prat Square and marched towards Cavancha beach against the government due to an increase in crime rates, homicides, and uncontrolled migration in the area, including the aggression suffered by two police officers attacked by Venezuelan migrants in the Cavancha beach (coded separately). Protesters marched with balloons and chants, some of them offensive towards migrants as they stated that the migration crisis is the cause of the security problems. A foreign citizen argued with the protesters and had to be removed from the beach by police. It is not clear if the man was attacked. A group of demonstrators went to a sector of the city where a group of Venezuelans were living in tents but police evicted them the day before. About 3,000 protesters arrived at the Las Rosas Airport, a place where foreign citizens who cross the Chilean border usually spend the night, and police had to arrive at the area to avoid confrontations. A motorcade was held towards Cavancha and Playa Brava areas.

On 8 March 2023, in San Pedro de Atacama (Antofagasta), thousands of women and LGBT+ community members marched at the main square to demand women's rights, the end of gender violence and discrimination against indigenous women, immigrant women and LGBT+ communities in the context of International Women's day.

On 16 January 2024, in Laguna Verde (Valparaiso), a large group of residents protested outside the town hall to demand that the municipality complete a survey of households lacking drinking water (via FIBE forms). A court had ordered the municipality to provide water in September 2022, but only around 5% of inhabitants were receiving it. Protesters also expressed frustration with water pollution in the area and the lack of municipal bus services.

On 13 February 2019, Students of Norte de Santander protested in the streets of Cucuta against the forced recruitment of children by armed groups in the region. Nearly 2000 gathered together and walked to the Fundadores square.

On 1 January 2020, in front of La Troja in Barranquilla, there was a clash between 2,000 people who were trying to enter a local store and Mobile Anti-Disturbance Squadron (ESMAD) officers. ESMAD officers fired tear gas to disperse the 2,000 people. Nearby local stores were vandalized.

On 8 February 2021, in Riosucio, Choco department, nearly 1,000 farmers from the rural areas gathered to protest against the eradication of coca plants. The group claimed coca is currently their only means of income and demanded improvements on the social and economic infrastructure before the destruction of illegal crops. The protest lasted two days.

On 4 January 2022, in La Pesquera (Arauca), some 1,200 people participated in an anti-war protest to reject the violent events that left at least 27 people dead two days before (coded separately) and to demand protection from the government and peace for their territory.

On 10 January 2023, in Bogota (Bogota, D.C.), around 5,000 people caravanned in protest through the streets of the city to protest against the change in the vehicle circulation restriction measures issued by local authorities. They also protested against the increase in fuel prices, the bad state of roads and the increase in the price of public transportation tickets.

On 8 February 2024, in Cucuta - Central (Norte de Santander), around 1,000, people including teachers, members of the Central Union of Workers (CUT), and supporters of President Gustavo Petro (PH), marched from the premises of the Norte de Santander Teachers Association (ASINORT) in El Contento neighborhood to the National Palace in the context of nationwide demonstrations called by President Petro and FECODE to demand the election of a new Prosecutor General. The demonstrators also condemned the raid by the prosecution on the FECODE headquarters in Bogota for suspected irregular financing of Petro's presidential campaign.

On 20 January 2019, in San Jose, 5,000 Nicaraguans protested to demand democracy in Nicaragua. It is reported that the Nicaraguan Great Unity group in exile decided to protest to request the freedom of Nicaragua and the departure of president Daniel Ortega.
On 6 September 2020, in San Jose , San Jose, thousands of protesters, mostly women, marched to demand a halt in femicides around the country.

On 26 November 2021, in San Jose, San Jose, a large number of Costa Rican women, including relatives of members of women victim of aggression, protested in front of the Supreme Court of Justice in the capital. The protest was joined by a group of Nicaraguan women who denounced the imprisonment of women in Nicaragua as an act of violence. The protest took place as part of the actions to commemorate the International Day for Non-Violence against Women, with protesters demanding more punitive justice for violence against women.

On 16 August 2022, in San Jose, Hospitales, San Jose, thousands of students of the five national public universities and administrative workers staged a protest and marched from the University of Costa Rica to the Presidential House in Zapote. People protested against cuts proposed to the education budget, known as FEES (Special Fund for Superior Education).

On 8 March 2023, in San Jose, San Jose, around 2500 of women staged a demonstration on the occasion of the International Women's Day in the San Jose Central Park. Women marched around the main avenues. Women demanded justice for the victims of femicide, respect for their reproductive health rights and labor rights, for the approval of abortion and against abuse, harassment, and violence. Dozens of Nicaraguan women joined the demonstration and demanded justice for the crimes committed by the current regime. A group of women set on fire a photo of the President, and another vandalized some walls of the National Public Museum by spraying graffiti. Also participated in the demonstration around 31 civil society organizations, including Colectivo Volcanicas, Feminist League of Nicaraguan Political Refugees, GOLEES foundation, Center for Justice and International Law, Las Rojas organization, among others, including a former member of parliament. A counter-demonstration by pro-life groups of around 20 people was staged in front of the Congress. Women threw paint at a member of the Liberal Progressive Party (PLP). Though demonstrators form the different groups had an encounter, no major incidents were reported.

On 8 March 2024, in San Jose, San Jose, thousands of women and members of women rights groups held a protest at the Plaza de la Democracia on the occasion of International Women's Day and to protest against continued lack of equality and against security issues facing women.

On 12 July 2019, in Santo Domingo, thousands of protesters gathered in front of Congress to protest against the President's plans to reform the Constitution so he can seek a third term. The protesters were mostly from the opposition PRM party, as well as from the FALPO, PRSD, and Common Good. Thousands of police officers guarded the area from early in the morning.
On 19 February 2020 in Santo Domingo, thousands of people dressed in black protested against the electoral board for canceling the municipal elections after the automated voting system failed.

On 12 August 2021, in Santo Domingo, Distrito Nacional, three thousand Haitian students staged a protest in front of the Haitian Embassy in Santo Domingo to demand their passports. Demonstrators claimed they made their requests 3 months earlier and the delay in the process has left them in an irregular situation.

On 7 September 2022, in Santo Domingo, Distrito Nacional, thousands of health workers held a march from the Dominican Medical College to the Social Security Treasury building to oppose the so called 87-01 Law of the Social Security System, and to demand better working conditions.

On 27 February 2023, in Santo Domingo, Distrito Nacional, a large group of supporters of the Modern Revolutionary Party led by the director of Metropolitan Office of Bus Services held a demonstration in support of the President Luis Abinader and called for his re-election close to the National Congress. The demonstration occurred when the President made his third presentation of accounts.

On 23 April 2024, in Santo Domingo, Distrito Nacional, thousands of teachers, led by the Dominican Professors Association (ADP), held a march and a sit-in protest with banners outside the Education Ministry demanding a 20 per cent increase in their salaries. This was part of a labor strike.

On 21 January 2019, in Quito - Eugenio Espejo (Pichincha), thousands of residents marched from Shyris avenue tribune against violence towards women for a second consecutive day. The protest took place after a woman was murdered by her husband in Ibarra and the police forces did not stop the act and another case of rape of a girl in Quito. Additionally, they protested against xenophobic behaviour of authorities and citizens against the Venezuelan community, because the man that killed his wife was of Venezuelan nationality.

On 6 March 2020, in Puyo, Pastaza, a thousand of indigenous women and members of the Confederation of Indigenous Nationalities of Ecuador (CONAIE) and Confederation of Indigenous Nationalities of the Ecuadorian Amazon (CONFENAIE) staged a demonstration in the main streets of the city as a commemoration of the International Women's Day.

On 10 May 2021, in Quito - Manuela Saenz (Pichincha), close to 3000 transport workers partners of the Quito Metropolitan District Transport Chamber (CTDMQ) marched from El Arbolito park towards the local government offices as a demonstration to reject the increasing cost of diesel prices and road biddings pushed by local authorities. In sectors of the city, approximately 70 transport workers that did not take part in their demonstration were attacked with rocks thrown to their busses. Windows were broken.

On 11 February 2022, in Loja (Loja), a considerable number of unionized teachers of the National Union of Educators (UNE) staged a demonstration in San Sebastian square to demand the government higher salaries and to re-hire teachers that were laid-off during the coronavirus pandemic.

On 27 April 2023, in Cuenca (Azuay), close to 5,000 people, made up of transport workers, university students, and various other labor groups in the Azuay region, gathered at the headquarters of the Cuenca drivers union and formed a caravan march to protest the poor road conditions in the Azuay region. The protesters marched for over 3 kilometers to demand urgent government intervention to address poor road infrastructure in the region. Over 100 labor organizations were present in the caravan.
On 8 March 2024, in Quito - Manuela Saenz (Pichincha), around 5,000 female residents marched towards San Francisco square as a demonstration to commemorate the International Women's Day.
On 28 January 2019, in San Salvador, 2000 people demonstrated peacefully against the privatization of water.

On 8 March 2020, in San Salvador (San Salvador), at least 3000 protesters, mostly women and members of women-centered organizations and networks gathered in front of the mall at at he 25 avenida norte of San Salvador to march towards the Gerardo Barrios square. They demanded the halt, investigation and punishment of gender-based violence. Also, members and supporters of the World March of Women gathered in front of the Christ of Peace to celebrate the 20 years of the organization, as well as to raise awareness of the inequalities affecting especially girls and women living with disability in El Salvador.

On 8 March 2021, in San Salvador, San Salvador, thousands of women marched on International Women's Day to demand the respect of women's rights and protest against femicides, transgender femicides and LGBT violence. They also demanded the government takes a more active role in safeguarding women's rights. Feminist organizations, artists, LGBT groups, ecofeminists, transfeminisms, journalists, students, indigenous and handicapped women participated in the march.

On 16 January 2022, in San Salvador, San Salvador, thousands of people staged an anti-government protest on the occasion of the 30th anniversary of the adoption of the peace accords of 1992. People also protested against the disappearance of people, the adoption of bitcoin as legal tender and the presidential re-election attempt. Protesters included civil society members, women, members of the LGBT community, students, water rights defenders, members of the evangelical church, former members of the military forces and of the FMLN, labor union affiliates, judges and magistrates

On 27 January 2023, in San Salvador, San Salvador, around 1,200 people staged a protest and marched from the Plaza Divino Salvador square park to the Presidential House. Demonstrators protested against the new pension Law, stating that affects their labour stability. The Union of Public Education Teachers of El Salvador (SIMEDUCO), CNTS, and Bases Magistrales participated in the protest, as well as teachers, police officers, social organizations, labour unions and associations. The protest was called 'Black March' (Marcha Negra). SIMEDUCO stated that around 10,000 teachers from Santa Ana, San Miguel, Cuscatlan, San Vicente, La Paz, Morazan and San Salvador participated I the protest.

On 29 June 2024, in San Salvador, San Salvador, more than 1000 members of the queer community held a march to celebrate their identity and demand equal rights and an end to discrimination based on gender identity or sexual orientation, as well as standing in solidarity with other oppressed people. The protesters also denounced the setbacks suffered in terms of recognition of their rights after measures such as the dissolution of the Directorate of Sexual Diversity, repeal of the decree prohibiting discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, exclusion from medical care, education, and the archiving of projects such as the gender identity law and the law of equality and non-discrimination. Upon arriving at the Salvador del Mundo square, the demonstrators met a group of foreigners from an evangelical church who, with banners in hand, accused the demonstrators of being sinners.
On 14 May 2019, around four thousand former military soldiers protested outside the Congress in Guatemala City claiming for improvements on their pensions.

On 18 January 2020, in Tecun Uman, San Marcos, a group of Honduran migrants clashed with police agents of Guatemala in the border with Mexico, trying to cross the border without following the new procedures for migrants. The rioters are part of more than 3,000 migrants that are crossing the border in a mass migratory caravan.

On 16 January 2021, in Vado Hondo, Chiquimula, an estimate of 3,500 Honduran migrants broke the military security fence to prevent the illegal passage of migrants. A member of the military forces was injured after a clash with migrants. Further clashes were reported on the following two consecutive days (coded separately).

On 20 May 2022, in Guatemala City, Guatemala, thousands of people staged a protest at the Main Campus of the University of San Carlos (UCSAC) in zone 12, against the election of Ms. Walter Mazariegos as the institution's dean. Protesters argue his election was a fraud. Students, professors, farmers members of CODECA, Indigenous Women of Palin, students', and teachers Associations, and labor unions related to the USAC participated in the protest. A group of hooded protesters blocked the access to the Agronomy School until a new ballot is organized.
On 12 May 2023, in Guatemala City, Guatemala, more than 1,000 merchants of the Market in zone 4 staged a demonstration in support of the local mayor (Unionist Party). Demonstrators marched to zone 1.

On 13 April 2024, in Chichicastenango, Quiche, a mob of around 2000 local inhabitants surrounded and torched a vehicle upon which four people, suspected of being robbers, were travelling. The victims died. The police was prevented from entering the scene, and is now investigating. 4 fatalities.
On 6 April 2019, around 5000 members of the Indignant Movement protested in Tegucigalpa demanding the resignation of Juan Orlando Hernandez.
On 27 February 2020, in Tegucigalpa, a massive crowd of students demonstrated to demand protection from the authorities.

On 1 May 2021, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, thousands of union members staged a march to commemorate International Workers Day marching to National Congress. People demanded better salaries and access to vaccines for all Hondurans. Teachers of the Pedagogic School, members of the Fesitranh and members of the LIBRE party participated in the march.

On 22 January 2022, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, thousands of supporters of the Liberty and Refoundation Party (LIBRE) and of the Savior Party of Honduras (PSH) blocked access to the National Congress (CN) in protest. The protesters denounced the provisional presidency of the National Congress elected on 21 January as illegitimate and want to avoid its officialization in the National Congress. The blockage ensued for two consecutive days.

On 10 January 2023, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, a group of representatives of at least 1,000 teachers who are about to retire protested in front of the Supreme Court of Justice (CSJ). They demanded government authorities to apply the 1980 retirement law, which was active when they were hired, rather than the current.

On 16 January 2024, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, a group of teachers from various departments across the country protested in front of the Secretariat of Education in the Government Civic Center (CCG) to demand the payment of back wages for unpaid extra-time hours. The teachers denounced that since 2007, approximately 1,200 teachers have been appointed with 30-hour shifts, but actually working 36.

On 5 January 2019, about 2000 persons, including members of the UP movement, demonstrated in front of the Government palace in Monterrey against the rise of the vehicle taxes and rates for public transport.
On 14 January 2020, in Ciudad de Mexico, nearly 8,000 transporters blocked various accesses to the city with 2,200 trucks in order to claim transport contracts.

On 7 January 2021, in San Quintin, Baja California, a thousand day workers of the San Marcos Invernaderos company started a strike. They used trucks to block accesses to the ranch in protest against delayed salary payments, including the Christmas bonus.

On 6 January 2022, in Chilpancingo de los Bravo, Guerrero, teachers from various regions demonstrated to demand the state government to provide more transparency on inclusion criteria for a horizontal promotion programme, from which thousands of qualifying teachers are being excluded. Recipients receive a 30 per cent economic stimulus.

On 2 January 2023, in Tapachula de Cordova y Ordonez, Chiapas, around 5000 migrants protested at the offices of the Mexican Commission of Aid to Refugees (Comar) to demanded solutions to the lack of procedures to request asylum.

On 7 January 2024, in Heroica Puebla de Zaragoza, Puebla, thousands of members of the Morena party from different parts of the state joined in protest against the migration of PRI candidates to the Morena party accusing them of linkages with the former President Pena Nieto and Calderon Hinojosa.

As reported on 17 June 2019, in the Santa Maria de Pantasma municipal area (Jinotega), local inhabitants partook in a mass to commemorate the death of Wiston Cornejo and to give thanks for the release of political prisoners. There was a strong police presence, but no clashes were reported.

On 21 March 2021, in Puerto Cabezas, Costa Caribe Norte, thousands of members of the YATAMA: Sons of Mother Earth Party, together with afrodescendents, staged a march against the lack of support from the government to deal with hurricanes and invasions of indigenous territories. Demonstrators called out for an electoral reform, the end to repression, the protection of natural resources as well as a decrease in agricultural-livestock activities.

On 30 September 2021, in La Chorrera, Panama Oeste, the educational community (including teachers, students of the school and their parents) of the school Moises Castillo Ocana marched towards the regional offices of the ministry of education demanding the completion of the works to rehabilitate the educational center. The school hosts around 2,000 students.

On 1 May 2022, in Panama City, Panama, thousands of workers organized in labor groups marched from the Porras Park to the Legislative Palace on the occasion of International Labor Day, denouncing the high cost of living and demanding an improvement in labor rights.

On 1 July 2023, in Panama City, Panama, more than 15,000 people staged a demonstration on occasion of Pride Month. Protesters demanded more rights for the LGBTI community, and in particular, for the approval of same-sex marriage.

On 6 April 2024, in Panama City, Panama, some people who were waiting in line to obtain voting cards at an event held by the Electoral Tribunal (TE) at a local school began to block the streets outside the school to demonstrate against the TE's decision to suddenly cancel the event for 'security reasons' due to overcrowding. According to a TE official, the event was intended for 400 people and there were more than 2,000 people in line. Demonstrators also surrounded several vehicles of TE employees.

On 9 May 2019, riots broke in the municipality of Itaugua after police tried to evict a group of people from private land. According to the sources, nearly 1000 police officers took part in the operation. Meanwhile, rioters set several objects on fire.

On 7 June 2020, in Salto del Guaira (Canindeyu), around 3,000 vehicles carried out a motorcade, led by the Association of Border's Unemployed (ADF), to draw attention to the crisis in the sector of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (Mipymes Association) and demand either a subsidy or the freezing of debts. The event took place under the context of the coronavirus pandemic and mandatory social isolation since March.

On 5 February 2021, in Asuncion (Asuncion), a large group gathered in Uruguay square and carried out a protest against President Mario Abdo, demanding him to provide answers about corruption cases and the government health expenditure during the coronavirus pandemic. The group claimed the country received a USD 1.6 million credit to fight the coronavirus. Protesters also marched towards the National Republican Association - Colorado Party (ANR-PC), calling it a corrupt party.
On 18 January 2022, in Ypane (Central), a significant amount of residents protested to demand more doctors to the Health Center and the creation of a district hospital.

On 17 January 2023, in Asuncion (Asuncion), a group of Indigenous people blocked Artigas street as part of a protest conducted by people who were camping outside the Paraguayan Institute of the Indigenous People (INDI). Many Indigenous communities have protested demanding that the INDI provides them with land, food kits, seeds, tools, and housing, among other demands.

On 4 March 2024, in Ciudad del Este (Alto Parana), thousands of people, including members of the Chamber of Commerce and Services, the Chamber of Entrepreneurs of Ciudad del Este and Alto Parana, and groups of workers marched to the old headquarters of the Judiciary to denounce the wave of crime that the city suffers, repudiate the action of judges for the release of criminals and to demand more significant police presence in the streets.

On 5 February 2019, more than 2000 handicraft miners protested in Abacay, demanding the director of a public mining company be removed from his position for inexperience and lack of knowledge of the sector's problems.

On 8 January 2020, in Callao city, more than 3700 health workers of Callao staged a demonstration outside the Daniel Alcides Carrion hospital, to demand better work conditions and better equipment in the hospital.

On 15 March 2021, in Nazca, Ica, a group of heavy transport workers members of the Nazca Transport Workers Union blocked the south Pan American highway and Aja bridge as part of a nationwide demonstration, called by the National Union of Transport Workers of Peru (UNT), against the raise in gasoline and toll prices.

On 11 January 2022, in Puno (Puno), a great number of residents of the Alto Puno sector and unionized civil construction workers staged a demonstration outside the land where the Altiplano hospital is being constructed to demand the company in charge to provide working positions for the residents. The union also demanded that at least 60% of construction workers be members of the union.

On 4 January 2023, in Huancayo (Junin), around 2000 residents marched through the city as a demonstration to demand the elimination of congress, calling for general elections and rejecting Dina Boluarte from being sworn as president. This was part of nation-wide demonstrations. Police officers intervened when they noticed demonstrators holding different tools that could be used for vandalism, which resulted in a brawl between police and demonstrators.

On 9 January 2024, in Juliaca (Puno), close to 10,000 local residents and from Ilave, Azangaro, Huacane, Puno, and other provinces, and family members of the victims of the riots of 2023 in the city marched through the city as a demonstration to demand justice in the case and the resignation of president Dina Boluarte. This demonstration was held as commemoration of the anniversary of the riots.
On 8 March 2019, in the centre of Montevideo, Municipio B, thousands of people marched for the International Day of the Woman, demanding the change of power balance and inequality of women.

On 8 March 2020, in Montevideo-Municipio B (Montevideo), thousands of women gathered in Cagancha Square, and on the esplanade of the University of the Republic, to demand women's rights and the end of gender violence on the International Women's Day march. The vice-president Argimon (PN: National Party) joined the protest.

On 8 March 2021, in Salto (Salto), a great amount of women gathered in in Artigas square and marched through Uruguay street in demand of women's rights and honoring a femicide victim, under the context of the International Women's day.

On 28 January 2022, in Montevideo (Montevideo), thousands of feminists marched from Independencia square towards Cagancha square to protest against the so-called 'rape culture' after a new abuse case took place in the previous week.

On 8 March 2023, in Montevideo (Montevideo), thousands of women marched from Libertad square as part of a demonstration in the context of International Women's day. They called for equality and an end to violence against women, among other demands. The groups Women in Black, Uruguayan Federation of Cooperatives for Mutual Aid, Where are Our Gurisas and Expresas Politicas participated in the march. The mayor of Montevideo (who is part of FA) and the City Director of Culture also took part in the action. The demonstrators burned their banners in front of the University of the Republic.

On 8 March 2024, in Montevideo (Montevideo), thousands of protestors, mostly women, marched through the city streets to the esplanade of the University of the Republic (UDELAR) to protest against discrimination and violence against women and demand improvements in the judicial system and labor conditions. The mobilization occurred on International Women's Day.
On 23 January 2019, in Guarenas, Miranda state, more than 2,000 members of the United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV) marched in support of the regime of President Nicolas Maduro.
On 9 January 2020, on the Libertador Avenue, Acarigua, Portuguesa state, residents protested due to the lack of potable water in the area. Around 20,000 residents are without water.

On 3 March 2021, in Ciudad Guayana (Bolivar state), an estimate of 2,000 workers from the Venezuelan steel corporation (Sidor) blocked the Guayana avenue in a protest to demand higher salaries, the implementation of their working benefits, and the reactivation of the steel industry, among other things. Protesters threatened to protest again if their demands were not met.
On 11 January 2022, in Barquisimeto (Lara), a large group of street merchants protested against new municipal rules prohibiting them from selling their goods on 20th Avenue and other areas downtown.

On 9 January 2023, in Valencia (Carabobo), a large group of demonstrators, including teachers, pensioners, and other labor group workers, protested to demand pay adjustments in accordance with the rising cost of living, and called for the renewal of their collective labor agreements. Some demonstrators demanded the repeal of the National Budget Office (ONAPRE) instruction. The protest was staged outside the Republica del Peru National School. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day, coinciding with the back-to-school day after the holidays.

On 9 January 2024, in Cumana (Sucre), thousands of demonstrators, including teachers, representatives of the FVM teachers' union, and an elected regional legislative council official belonging to the SPV political party, protested to demand better pay and working conditions, and respect for their labor rights. They gathered by the San Vicente de Paul Church and then marched around the city. This was one of the dozens of simultaneous nationwide demonstrations staged by teachers and other state workers that day.
